Oliver — thanks for the note and the SOW. Quick read-through below and copying Legal and Sales to align on an approval path.

High level response: we can consider a narrowly-scoped MFN and a channel preference, but both require explicit limits and guardrails:

1) MFN: acceptable only for list price applied to equivalent product tiers and not to promotional or transient partner discounts. We will propose a 24-month term with a cap (no retro pricing adjustments beyond 3% of documented list pricing) and audit windows limited to annual reviews.

2) Exclusivity / channel preference: Redwoods will not do full exclusivity for market segment; however, we can offer a prioritized channel path for pilot customers in North America for 12 months with explicit carve-outs for (a) customers under existing channel commitments, and (b) any enterprise customer bringing >$1m ARR in the first 12 months. We can include a first refusal on renewals within a 30-day window.

To move forward we need Executive clearance for: discounting flexibility (they have requested a 20% starter discount + potential performance rebate) and approval to agree the MFN language with the caps above. Ben — are the proposed redlines below workable from legal and risk perspective? Lauren / Marcus — any commercial objections?

I will attach our draft redline and the SOW for reference. If we can get a yes/no by EOD Wednesday I will get a counter back to Oliver with our changes.

Thanks,

Rafa / Lauren — reviewed Oliver's attachments and Rafael's proposed framework. Legal's view: we can accept the commercial contours with the following mandatory mitigations. I'm pasting the redline summary here to keep the thread simple. Full redline attached (redline_Nairn_term_sheet.docx).

Key legal constraints / recommended redlines:

- MFN scope: limit to direct list pricing for the exact product SKU set used in the PoC and for visible published list prices. Exclude (i) partner promotions, (ii) one-off discounts tied to integration commitments, and (iii) discounts tied to marketplace placements.
- MFN cap & remedy: MFN adjustments are limited to prospective pricing only; no retroactive credits. Put an overall cap equal to 5% of contract value for any pricing adjustments over the 24-month MFN window.
- Audit: audit rights limited to once per 12 months, scope limited to pricing documents/agreements only; Redwood may require redaction of customer-sensitive data.
- Exclusivity: disallow absolute exclusivity. Approve a limited "pilot preference" clause: 12-month preferential onboarding, but carve out existing channel agreements and enterprise carve-outs (we should enumerate a $1m ARR carve-out). Add a mutual escape clause if adoption metrics don't meet X (define X — suggest pilot activation for >= 20% of targeted deployments).
- Performance rebate vs. discount: prefer a performance-based rebate tied to consumption to limit prepaid revenue risk. If Sales insists on an upfront discount, cap total up-front discount exposure to 20% and require milestone payments.
- Approval path: any MFN or exclusivity variant that exceeds the caps above or extends beyond 24 months requires VP-level signoff (Lauren or Marcus) and a written exception from Legal + Finance.

If Sales can live with a performance rebate and the MFN carve-outs / cap above, Legal is comfortable with an approval memo we can sign-off on.

Ben Carter

Subject: Escalation: Exec sign-off requested — Nairn Energy MFN & channel preference

Lauren / Marcus — escalating for exec decision. Below is the short ask and my recommendation. Ben's legal mitigations are attached and summarized above (see his note).

Deal snapshot:
- Account: Nairn Energy (renewables monitoring)
- ARR: $1,200,000 first-year ARR (pilot + scale assumptions)
- Ask: MFN for 24 months, 20% upfront discount + potential performance rebate, and a 12-month channel preference (first refusal on renewals).
- Timeline: customer expects counters this week; procurement wants contractual language in SOW.

My recommendation (to propose to the customer):
1) Approve a limited MFN with Ben's carve-outs and a 5% adjustment cap; no retroactive credits.
2) Convert the 20% upfront discount into a 10% upfront + up to 10% performance rebate tied to usage thresholds over the first 12 months.
3) Grant a 12-month "pilot preference" (not exclusivity) with explicit carve-outs and a 30-day first-refusal window on renewals.

Decision options for Execs:
- APPROVE (Rafael's recommendation) — Sales can send counter with redlines and get handshake sign-off from Procurement.
- APPROVE WITH STRONGER GUARDRAILS — e.g., reduce upfront discount to 5% or shorten MFN to 12 months.
- DENY — ask for removal of MFN / exclusivity language entirely.

Please reply with APPROVE / APPROVE WITH CHANGES / DENY and any brief notes. If you want a one-pager I can prepare a succinct approval memo for signature. Time sensitive — customer expects response before Friday close of business.

Thanks,
